plugin.name: AI Bridge
plugin.description:
Bring Claude Code into your JetBrains IDE for everyday development. Explore your codebase, plan changes and review proposed edits from the same workspace where you write code.

Features

  • Work with project context. Send selected code or the current file to a conversation with Alt+K, and preview the context before submitting a message.
  • Review changes in the IDE. Inspect proposed edits in the native diff viewer and open related files and terminals directly.
  • Organize your work. Use separate chat tabs, task templates and project queues. Reorder pending messages or combine them while the current task continues.
  • Keep useful conversations. Search past messages, save bookmarks and record decision notes.
  • Recover from dropped connections. Temporary network and server errors are retried automatically, and the reply continues where it stopped.
  • Control long-running tasks. Set project concurrency limits, monitor local CPU and memory usage, and reduce background rendering with low resource mode.
  • Choose how Claude works. Select the model and reasoning effort, schedule messages and configure automatic continuation after usage limits.
  • Use your preferred language. The interface includes English and Turkish.

Requirements and setup

Use a JetBrains IDE based on IntelliJ Platform 2023.1 or newer with a JCEF-enabled runtime, Node.js and an installed, configured Claude Code CLI. Open the plugin from the Tools menu or press Ctrl+Shift+C to start a conversation.

Use your existing Claude Code authentication or provider configuration. Messages, code context and tool requests are processed through the provider and services you configure; their usage terms and charges apply.

About

Independently maintained by Birkan Kader. Claude and Claude Code are Anthropic products. This plugin is not an official Anthropic or JetBrains product.

License

plugin.change-notes:
0.36 - AI Bridge (2026-10-05)

  • The plugin is now called AI Bridge and has a new logo. Its ID, settings and conversations are unchanged, so it updates in place.
  • Windows: new chats start faster because the process guard is compiled once and reused instead of being rebuilt for every chat.

0.35 - Claude Code Workspace (2026-10-05)

  • The plugin is now called Claude Code Workspace. Its ID, settings and conversations are unchanged, so it updates in place.
  • Dropped connections ("The socket connection was closed unexpectedly", reset or stalled streams) and temporary server errors are retried automatically with growing delays, and the reply continues where it stopped.
  • A retry shows as one compact line with a countdown instead of an error message; the provider's full text is one click away.
  • When retries run out, a small banner confirms the conversation is kept and continues it on request.
  • A blinking "Thinking" indicator with the elapsed time replaces the random status words.
  • Claude starts in the background while you type, so the first message of a chat no longer waits for the CLI to launch.
  • The message box stays usable after errors; error banners have clear titles and can be dismissed.
  • Code review fixes: Escape closes menus without stopping the task, a rejected message keeps its text and attachments, permission and plan questions stay with their chat until answered, older chats open directly, delete and rename use the right project, failed settings saves are reported, the Stop button stays visible while typing and the mode menu fits narrow panels.

0.34 - Claude Code for Kasif (2026-09-24)

  • Support IntelliJ IDEA 2023.1 and newer with Java 17 compatible plugin classes.

0.33 - Claude Code for Kasif (2026-09-17)

  • Queue multiple messages while a task is running and keep the active task uninterrupted.
  • Reorder queued messages or merge selected messages with their attachments.
  • Review the compact queue above the composer and restore it when reopening a chat.

0.31 - Claude Code for Kasif (2026-09-15)

  • Auto-resume on usage limit is enabled by default for new or unset preferences.
  • Saved global, project and session choices remain unchanged, including explicit opt-outs.
  • Automatic resume waits for the initial settings load before acting on its default.

0.3 - Claude Code for Kasif (2026-09-14)

  • Plugin updates are available through the custom repository at https://birkankader.com/plugins/kasif/updatePlugins.xml.
  • Add the repository once in IDE plugin settings to receive future updates without manually installing ZIP files.
  • Each release includes a matching source archive and SHA-256 checksums.

0.2 - Claude Code for Kasif (2026-09-11)

  • Automatic recovery from API errors and model-aware context budgets with compact and continue.
  • New messages preserve the active task; only the latest pending message is sent after it finishes.
  • Session settings use a JSON file to preserve valid settings through Windows CLI launchers.

0.1 - Claude Code for Kasif (2026-09-09)

Developer and publisher: Birkan Kader.

  • Chat tabs with a permanent new-tab button and Turkish interface.
  • Low resource mode, task controls and local resource metrics.
  • Conversation search, bookmarks, decision notes and task templates.
  • Context preview, scheduled messages and automatic resume.
  • Model-specific reasoning effort, applied reliably on the next message.
  • Correct context usage percentages and draft estimates that distinguish file references from later file reads.
  • Rapid prompts share one new conversation; failed sends preserve editor context on retry and report CLI write failures.
  • Closed tabs retain process ownership until exit; Windows cleanup uses at most two asynchronous commands.
  • IDE exit requests backend cleanup over RPC; disposed processes and WebView connections cannot restart.
  • Helper CLI commands participate in shutdown; cancelled MCP probes retain their slots until bounded process cleanup finishes.
  • Session switching and reconnects restore history; disconnected sends show errors without simulated responses.
  • Project-owned selection delivery and background retry avoid duplicate work and blocking cleanup on the UI thread.
  • Incremental CLI output decoding preserves split UTF-8 characters and avoids repeatedly scanning long incomplete lines.
  • Chat titles refresh tab presentation without VFS rename events, preserving Java inspection settings.
  • Moved tabs transfer native callbacks to their current panel; closed panels discard queued notifications on the UI thread.
  • MCP discovery runs only when its panel opens, with two concurrent detail probes at most.
  • Bounded IntelliJ repaint scheduling and stream diagnostics; duplicate session starts and Bash hook recursion guarded.
  • Fewer duplicate CLI initialization processes, non-blocking Windows metadata cleanup and startup timings.
  • Auto-resume toggle works before the first message; pending resumes survive failed sends and reconnects.
